mechanism_narrative: A higher unemployment rate (UNRATE) is associated with lower S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days, as a weakening labor market typically leads to reduced corporate earnings and increased risk aversion.
failure_condition: The Rank IC for UNRATE as a predictor of 20d returns is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) rises above 0.5%, it signals an imminent monetary tightening cycle that increases discount rates and compresses equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: FEDFUNDS > 0.5% occurs in more than 30% of the time, but 5d returns are negative in less than 40% of those instances.

mechanism_narrative: A combination of rising consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) above 0.5% month-over-month and falling industrial production (INDPRO) below 1.0% month-over-month signals an inflationary supply shock that increases cost pressures and reduces corporate margins, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The interaction condition (CPIAUCSL > 0.5% and INDPRO < -1.0%) occurs in more than 20% of the time, but 20d returns are negative in less than 40% of those instances.

mechanism_narrative: In a late-cycle expansion regime (defined by GDP growth above 2.0% and unemployment rate below 4.0%), a federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) above 2.0% signals an imminent monetary tightening that leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: In the late-cycle expansion regime (GDPC1 > 2.0% and UNRATE < 4.0%), FEDFUNDS > 2.0% occurs in more than 30% of the time, but 60d returns are negative in less than 40% of those instances.

mechanism_narrative: A positive month-over-month change in housing starts (HOUST) signals a strengthening housing market, which is a leading indicator of economic growth and predicts positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The positive month-over-month change in HOUST occurs in more than 50% of the time, but 20d returns are positive in less than 40% of those instances.

mechanism_narrative: When industrial production (INDPRO) falls below 100.0 (index 2017=100), it signals a contraction in the manufacturing sector that leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: INDPRO < 100.0 occurs in more than 30% of the time, but 5d returns are negative in less than 40% of those instances.

mechanism_narrative: A combination of rising unemployment rate (UNRATE) above 5.0% and falling employment (PAYEMS) below 138000.0 (thousands) signals a deteriorating labor market, which typically leads to reduced consumer spending and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The condition (UNRATE > 5.0% AND PAYEMS < 138000.0) occurs in more than 20% of the time, but 20d returns are negative in less than 40% of those instances.

mechanism_narrative: In a supply contraction regime (INDPRO < 100.0 and HOUST < 1000.0), a rising consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) above 0.5% month-over-month signals an inflationary supply shock that increases cost pressures and reduces corporate margins, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: In the supply contraction regime (INDPRO < 100.0 and HOUST < 1000.0), CPIAUCSL > 0.5% (mo-mo) occurs in more than 20% of the time, but 60d returns are negative in less than 40% of those instances.
